claims.text: Tungsten carbide-based cermets will mitigate corrosion and wear during long-term contact with high-temperature molten aluminum.
Molten-aluminum-contacting rollers and guide plates are conventionally made from steel or iron-based alloys.
Steel or iron-based components corrode rapidly in molten aluminum.
Tungsten carbide-based cermet parts can be fabricated by powder metallurgy or infiltration techniques.
Typical molten-aluminum operating temperatures for this application are approximately 680–710 °C.
Tungsten carbide phases in the cermet remain stable during prolonged exposure to molten aluminum.
Tungsten carbide phases are chemically inert toward molten aluminum.
The stability and chemical inertness of tungsten carbide reduce reactions and intermetallic formation at the material–aluminum interface.
Reduced reactivity with aluminum slows dissolution and chemical attack of the cermet parts.
Slower dissolution and chemical attack reduce corrosion and erosion of molten-aluminum-contacting parts.
Tungsten carbide-based cermet components will have significantly longer service life than iron- or steel-based components.
The expected service-life extension is approximately twofold to threefold.
The production cost and specialized fabrication requirements of cermets could limit their widespread use.
Long-term field-performance data for tungsten carbide-based cermets under extreme molten-aluminum service conditions are limited.
